faq.q: What kinds of moves do you handle?
faq.a: We handle local residential moves, Texas intrastate moves, office and commercial relocations, packing, short-term storage and specialty items including pianos and antiques.

faq.q: Are you a full-service mover?
faq.a: Yes. We handle the whole job—packing, protecting furniture and floors, loading, transport, unloading and placing everything in the right rooms. You can also choose just the parts you need.

faq.q: Can you handle a difficult move?
faq.a: Yes—hard moves are where an experienced crew shows. Third-floor walk-ups, narrow bungalow doors, small elevators, pianos and long Hill Country driveways are all part of the job. Tell us about the access at both ends and we plan the crew and equipment around it.

faq.q: Are you licensed and insured?

faq.q: How is my estimate calculated?
faq.a: We consider the size of your move, access at both locations, travel distance, crew needs and optional services. Call or send your details for a personalized estimate.

faq.q: How far do you travel for local moves?
faq.a: We serve Austin and every town south along I-35, including Buda and Kyle, plus communities within about 30 miles of our Buda office. For longer distances we handle moves anywhere within Texas.

faq.q: Do you move outside Austin?
faq.a: Yes. We serve Greater Austin and Central Texas, and we move customers anywhere within the state of Texas.

faq.q: Can you help with packing?
faq.a: Yes. Our crews arrive with moving essentials and can help with packing, shrink-wrapping and protecting floors, walls and delicate belongings.

apartment-movers-austin.html.h1: Apartment movers who make the stairs look easy.
apartment-movers-austin.html.lede: Full-service apartment and condo moves across Austin, Buda, Kyle and San Marcos—walk-ups, elevators, tight halls and all.
apartment-movers-austin.html.article:
## Apartment moves are access moves

The furniture in most apartments fits on one truck. What decides how long the move takes is everything between the truck and your door: the parking lot, the gate, the stairs or elevator, the hallway and the doorway. We plan around those details from the first call.

### Walk-ups and stairs

Third-floor walk-ups are routine for an experienced crew. We protect railings and landings, take heavy pieces apart when that's safer, and carry rather than drag. Tell us the floor and whether the stairs have tight turns.

### Elevators and loading areas

Many Austin apartment and condo buildings require you to reserve the elevator or loading dock for a set window, and some ask for a certificate of insurance from the mover before move day. Get the rules from the leasing office in writing and share them with us when you book.

### Moving out without losing your deposit

- Ask for floor and doorway protection in shared hallways
- Photograph each room once it's empty
- Return keys, gate remotes and parking tags the way your lease requires
- Leave time for a final clean before the walkthrough

### Apartment to house, or house to apartment

Moving up to a house or downsizing into an apartment? We pack, move and place everything room by room, and can coordinate short-term storage if your dates don't line up. See [packing services](packing-services-austin.html) and [storage between homes](moving-storage-austin.html).

side.title: Tell us about your building
side.text: These details set the crew size and timing.

faq.q: Do you move studios and small apartments?
faq.a: Yes—studios, one-bedrooms and large condos across Austin and along I-35.

faq.q: What if my building has no elevator?
faq.a: Stairs and walk-ups are routine for our crews. Tell us the floor and any tight turns when you request a quote so we plan the right crew.

faq.q: What if my building needs a certificate of insurance?
faq.a: Share the building's requirements, including any exact wording they need, when you book. We'll confirm what's needed before moving day.

furniture-movers-austin.html.h1: Heavy, awkward and precious furniture, handled.
furniture-movers-austin.html.lede: Sectionals, armoires, dining sets, beds and family heirlooms—wrapped, protected and, when it helps, taken apart and put back together.
furniture-movers-austin.html.article:
## The right way to move big furniture

Most furniture damage happens at doorways, corners and on stairs—not on the road. Good furniture moving comes down to protection, the right equipment and knowing when a piece should come apart.

### Wrapped before it moves

Upholstery, wood finishes and glass are wrapped in moving pads or plastic before they leave the room, and floors and door frames along the path are protected.

### Disassembly and reassembly

Bed frames, dining tables, desks and some sectionals travel more safely in pieces. Tell us in advance which items will need it so the crew brings the right tools and time. Hardware stays bagged and labeled with its piece.

### When it won't fit

Measure doorways, hallways, stair turns and elevator depth at the new home before moving day. Removing legs, feet or doors often solves a tight fit—tell us about anything that looks close.

### Heirlooms and antiques

Delicate finishes, old joinery and pieces with sentimental value get extra padding and an unhurried carry. For pianos, clocks and fine china, see [piano and specialty moving](piano-moving-austin.html).

side.title: Measure before you move
side.text: A tape measure now saves surprises later.

faq.q: How is furniture protected during the move?
faq.a: Pieces are wrapped in pads or plastic before they move, and floors and doorways along the path are protected.

faq.q: Can you move antiques and heirlooms?
faq.a: Yes. Delicate and valuable pieces get extra care—tell us about them up front so we can plan.

moving-storage-austin.html.h1: When your moving dates don’t line up.
moving-storage-austin.html.lede: Closing delayed? Lease ending before the new place is ready? We coordinate short-term storage so your move happens in two easy steps instead of one stressful one.
moving-storage-austin.html.article:
## Storage coordination for in-between moves

Moves don't always happen on one clean date. A closing slips, a renovation runs long or a lease ends a week early. Instead of rushing, we coordinate short-term storage so your belongings are packed, protected and waiting until the new home is ready.

### How it works

1. Tell us both dates: when you need to be out and when you can move in.
2. We plan the move-out and the delivery as two parts of the same job.
3. Your belongings go into storage, then come to the new home when you're ready.

### What to keep out of storage

- Medication, documents and valuables
- Anything you'll need in the meantime: seasonal clothes, work gear, school items
- Perishable, flammable or hazardous items

### Get it in writing

Storage adds a second moving day. Ask how storage, access and delivery will be handled, and make sure every part is in your written proposal.

side.text: We'll plan both halves of the move together.
items: Items you'll need in the meantime

faq.q: Do you offer storage?
faq.a: We coordinate short-term storage between homes as part of your move. Tell us your dates and we'll plan the move-out and delivery together.

faq.q: How long can my things stay in storage?
faq.a: It depends on your dates and the storage arrangement—ask when you request your quote so it's spelled out in writing.

faq.q: What shouldn't go into storage?
faq.a: Medication, documents, valuables, anything you'll need before move-in, and perishable, flammable or hazardous items.

moving-quotes-texas.html.h1: How moving quotes work in Texas.
moving-quotes-texas.html.lede: Binding or not-to-exceed, what changes the price, and why stairs and parking matter—explained by a licensed Texas mover.
moving-quotes-texas.html.article:
## What Texas requires

Licensed Texas movers must give you a written proposal before loading anything. It's either **binding**—the exact price of the move—or **not-to-exceed**—the most you can be charged. It should also say when payment is due and which payment methods are accepted. Source: [TxDMV](https://www.txdmv.gov/motorists/consumer-protection/dont-make-a-move).

## What changes the price of a move

- **How much is moving.** More furniture and boxes means more time, and sometimes a bigger crew or truck.
- **Access at both homes.** Stairs, elevators, long walks from the truck and tight doorways all take time.
- **Distance.** Local moves are mostly about time; Texas moves add the drive.
- **Extra services.** Packing, disassembly and specialty items such as pianos.
- **Timing.** End-of-month and summer dates are the busiest.

## Do movers charge extra for stairs?

Stairs take more time and effort, so they usually affect the price—either as a line item or through the time the move takes. The fair way to handle it is up front: tell your mover about every staircase, elevator and long carry at both addresses so the written proposal reflects the real job.

## How to get an accurate quote

Be specific. List large furniture, mention anything heavy or fragile, share photos of tricky access and give both full addresses. Surprises on moving day are what make final prices differ from expectations.

## Comparing quotes side by side

Is each quote binding or not-to-exceed? Does it include packing materials, disassembly and the drive? Is the mover's TxDMV certificate active? The lowest number isn't the best deal if it leaves things out. For more, see [10 questions to ask a mover](questions-to-ask-movers.html).

side.title: Before you compare
side.text: Check every quote for these.

faq.q: What's the difference between a binding and a not-to-exceed proposal?
faq.a: A binding proposal states the exact price. A not-to-exceed proposal states the maximum you can be charged. Texas movers must give you one in writing before loading.

faq.q: Do movers charge extra for stairs?
faq.a: Stairs add time and effort, so they usually affect the price. Mention every staircase and elevator at both addresses so your written proposal reflects the real job.

faq.q: Why do moving quotes vary so much?
faq.a: Movers make different assumptions about time, crew size and access. The more detail you share, the closer quotes get to each other—and to the final price.

faq.q: Is the ballpark estimator on this site a quote?
faq.a: No. It gives a planning range only. Your personal written estimate is based on the details of your move.

questions-to-ask-movers.html.h1: Ten questions to ask before you hire a mover.
questions-to-ask-movers.html.lede: The right questions sort the professionals from the risks in a single phone call. Here's what to ask—and the answers to listen for.
questions-to-ask-movers.html.article:
### 1. What's your TxDMV certificate number?

Every household mover in Texas needs an active certificate. Check it in the state's Truck Stop database. Ours is #000572890B.

### 2. Will I get a written proposal before you load?

The answer must be yes—Texas requires it. Be wary of anyone who only quotes by phone.

### 3. Is the price binding or not-to-exceed?

Binding is the exact price; not-to-exceed is the maximum. Either is fine, as long as you know which one you have.

### 4. What could change the final price?

Listen for clear answers about time, stairs, access and extra services—not vague reassurance.

### 5. What's your liability for damage, and can I increase it?

Texas lets you and the mover agree on liability before the move. Some agreements limit it to 60 cents per pound per item. That isn't insurance, so ask about options and consider your own coverage.

### 6. Who will actually do my move?

Ask whether the company's own crew handles the job from start to finish.

### 7. How do you protect my home and furniture?

Pads, wrap, floor and doorway protection should be standard answers.

### 8. What happens if my dates change?

Closings slip. Ask how changes are handled and whether storage can be coordinated.

### 9. How do I reach you on moving day?

You want a real person on the phone, not a call center. Our phone is answered daily, 8am to 5pm.

### 10. How do claims work if something is damaged?

In Texas you file a written claim within 90 days of delivery, and TxDMV offers free mediation if you and the mover can't agree. See [how Texas protects your move](austin-movers.html).

side.title: Red flags
side.text: Walk away if you see these.
items: No TxDMV number, or an inactive one
A price far below everyone else's

faq.q: How do I check a mover's license in Texas?
faq.a: Ask for the TxDMV certificate number and look it up in TxDMV's Truck Stop database. It should say Active.

faq.q: Where can I file a complaint about a mover?
faq.a: With TxDMV online, by calling 1-888-368-4689 or by emailing TruckStop@TxDMV.gov. Moves that cross state lines are handled by the federal FMCSA instead.

faq.q: Should I pay a large deposit up front?
faq.a: Read the written proposal: it should state when payment is due and how. Be cautious with any mover that won't put payment terms in writing.

moving-glossary.html.lede: The words you'll see on Texas moving quotes, contracts and building rules—explained without the jargon.
moving-glossary.html.article:
### Binding proposal

A written price for the move that won't change, as long as the job matches what was described.

### Not-to-exceed proposal

A written proposal that sets the maximum you can be charged. The final bill can be lower, not higher.

### Moving services contract

The agreement you sign before loading. In Texas, the written proposal becomes part of it, and you get a signed copy at delivery.

### TxDMV certificate

The license every household mover operating within Texas must hold from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles. Check it in the Truck Stop database.

### Intrastate vs. interstate

An intrastate move stays inside Texas and is regulated by TxDMV. An interstate move crosses state lines and is regulated by the federal FMCSA.

### Liability (valuation)

How much the mover will pay if something is lost or damaged. In Texas it's agreed before the move—some agreements limit it to 60 cents per pound per item. It isn't insurance.

### Inventory

An optional list of items and their condition, signed before and after the move. Useful if you ever need to file a claim.

### Claim

A written request for payment for loss or damage. In Texas, file it within 90 days of delivery.

### Certificate of insurance (COI)

A document many apartment, condo and office buildings require from a mover before move day, showing the mover's insurance coverage.

### Elevator or dock reservation

A booked time window for using a building's freight elevator or loading dock.

### Long carry

When the truck has to park far from the door, so everything is carried a long way. Mention it when you request a quote.

### Right-of-way permit

In Austin, a City permit that may be required to park a moving truck in a metered space, curb lane, alley or sidewalk. Call 3-1-1 for details.

### Full-service move

The mover handles the whole job: packing, protection, loading, transport, unloading and placing items in the right rooms.

### Partial packing

The crew packs only certain rooms or items—often the kitchen and fragile pieces—while you pack the rest.

side.text: Keep reading.

faq.q: Is a moving company's liability the same as insurance?
faq.a: No. Liability is what the mover agrees to pay for loss or damage under your contract. You can buy separate insurance for more protection.

faq.q: Which agency regulates my move?
faq.a: If it stays within Texas, the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles. If it crosses state lines, the federal FMCSA.

house-movers-austin.html.article:
## A house is a lot of moves at once

Bedrooms, kitchen, garage, patio, attic: every part of a house moves differently. We plan the crew, truck and timing around the whole property, not just the furniture count.

### What full service includes

- Packing as much or as little as you want, with materials supplied
- Pads, wrap and floor protection at both homes
- Disassembly and reassembly of beds, tables and other large pieces
- Loading, transport, unloading and placing everything room by room

### Garages, sheds and patios

Tools, yard equipment, grills and outdoor furniture often get left for last—and take longer than expected. Tell us what's outside so it's in the plan. Empty fuel and propane before moving day; flammable items can't ride on the truck.

### Difficult houses are our specialty

Split levels, narrow bungalow doors, long Hill Country driveways and steep stairs are where an experienced crew shows. Mention them when you request a quote and we'll plan around them.

See also: [packing services](packing-services-austin.html), [furniture moving](furniture-movers-austin.html) and [storage between homes](moving-storage-austin.html).

side.title: For an accurate quote
side.text: These details shape the crew and truck.

faq.q: How long does it take to move a house?
faq.a: It depends on the size of the home, how much is packed and the access at both ends. Your written proposal will spell out the plan and crew.

faq.q: Do you pack the whole house?
faq.a: We can pack everything, just the kitchen and fragile items, or nothing at all—your choice.

faq.q: Do you move garage and outdoor items?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us what's in the garage, shed and patio so it's included in the plan. Fuel and propane must be emptied first.

small-moves-austin.html.h1: Small moves, handled with the same care.
small-moves-austin.html.lede: A studio, a single room, a storage unit or a few heavy pieces—moved by the same experienced crew we send on whole-house jobs.
small-moves-austin.html.article:
## When a small move makes sense

Not every move fills a truck. Small moves are common when you're moving into a furnished place, splitting a household, clearing a storage unit or bringing home a few big purchases.

### Typical small moves

- Studios and small apartments
- A single room or a home office
- Moving items out of, or into, a storage unit
- A sofa, dresser or appliance between homes

### Small doesn't mean simple

A single sleeper sofa up a third-floor walk-up can be harder than a dozen boxes on the ground floor. Tell us exactly what's moving and how the access looks at both ends, and we'll plan the right crew.

### Make it efficient

Have everything in one place, boxes packed and taped, and parking cleared before the crew arrives. Small moves go fastest when nothing needs to be gathered on the day.

side.title: Tell us
side.text: A quick list is all we need.

faq.q: Do you take small moves?

last-minute-movers-austin.html.h1: Last-minute move? Call, and we’ll tell you straight.
last-minute-movers-austin.html.lede: Closings move, leases end early and plans change. When the clock is short, a real person answers our phone daily from 8am to 5pm.
last-minute-movers-austin.html.article:
## Why short-notice moves happen

A buyer wants an early closing. A lease falls through. A job starts sooner than planned. Short-notice moves are stressful because every decision has to happen at once.

### What to do first

1. Call us at [(512) 443-6141](tel:+15124436141)—a phone call is faster than any form.
2. Have both addresses, the size of the move and your deadline ready.
3. Tell us what's already packed and what isn't.

### How we help when time is short

We'll tell you honestly what we can do on your timeline. If the full move can't happen on your date, options like packing help, moving the essentials first or coordinating short-term storage can keep you on schedule.

### Save time on your end

- Pack an essentials bag for each person
- Book elevators and parking as soon as you have a date
- Set aside anything that isn't coming so it isn't loaded by mistake

See [storage between homes](moving-storage-austin.html) and [packing services](packing-services-austin.html).

side.title: Have this ready
side.text: It speeds up the first call.

faq.q: Can you move me this week?
faq.a: Call us at (512) 443-6141. We'll check availability right away and tell you honestly what's possible.

faq.q: What if I haven't packed?
faq.a: Our crew can pack for you. Tell us how much is unpacked so we plan the time.

faq.q: Is calling faster than the online form?
faq.a: Yes. For short-notice moves, a call during business hours gets you an answer fastest.

loading-unloading-help.html.h1: Loading and unloading help from people who do it every day.
loading-unloading-help.html.lede: Renting your own truck or using a moving container? Our crew loads it tight, pads it right and unloads it safely at the other end.
loading-unloading-help.html.article:
## Why loading matters more than driving

Most damage in a do-it-yourself move happens inside the truck: furniture shifts, boxes crush and unpadded pieces rub together on the highway. A well-loaded truck uses every inch, keeps heavy items low and locks the load in place.

### Rental trucks and moving containers

Whether it's a rental truck or a portable container, the job is the same: heavy and square items first, tall pieces tied off, boxes stacked by weight and every gap filled. Tell us the size of the truck or container so we bring the right crew.

### Unloading at the other end

We can unload and place furniture and boxes in the right rooms, and reassemble pieces we took apart.

### Before the crew arrives

- Have the truck or container parked as close to the door as possible
- Pack and seal boxes, and label them by room
- Have pads, straps and a dolly in the truck if the rental includes them

Prefer a full-service move instead? See [house moving](house-movers-austin.html).

side.title: Tell us

faq.a: Yes. Tell us the size and where it will be parked, and we'll plan the crew.

faq.q: Do you unload at the destination too?
faq.a: Yes, if the destination is within our service area. Let us know both locations when you book.

faq.q: Who drives the truck?
faq.a: With labor-only help, you drive your rental. For a move where we handle the transport too, see our full-service moves.

senior-moving-austin.html.h1: Senior moves, done patiently and with respect.
senior-moving-austin.html.lede: Moving out of a long-time family home is about more than furniture. We take the time to pack carefully, place things just right and keep the day calm.
senior-moving-austin.html.article:
## A different kind of move

A senior move often means leaving a home of many years, deciding what goes and what stays, and fitting a lifetime into a smaller space. The pace should fit the person, not the truck.

### Plan the new space first

Measure the new rooms and decide where the bed, favorite chair and dresser will go before moving day. A simple floor plan lets the crew place furniture exactly where it belongs.

### Downsizing in stages

- Start with rooms that are used least
- Set aside keepsakes and photos for family first
- Decide on donations and sales well before the move
- Pack daily essentials, medication and documents separately

### On moving day

We can pack, protect and move everything, then set up the bed and key furniture so the first night in the new home feels familiar. Family members are welcome to coordinate by phone—tell us who to call.

### Assisted living and retirement communities

Many communities have move-in windows, elevator reservations and rules about what can go in the hallways. Get them in writing and share them with us early.

student-movers.html.h1: Student moves without the borrowed-pickup drama.
student-movers.html.lede: Dorms and apartments near UT Austin and Texas State in San Marcos—moved quickly, carefully and on the tight schedules that semesters demand.
student-movers.html.article:
## Semester moves are all about timing

Leases start and end on the same few days, move-in windows are short and elevators are booked solid. The earlier you lock in a date, the easier it gets.

### Apartments and dorms

Many student apartment buildings set move-in hours and require elevator or loading-dock reservations. Some ask for a certificate of insurance from the mover. Get the rules from the leasing office early and share them with us.

### Parents moving students from out of town

You can book and coordinate by phone. Tell us who'll be at the apartment to let the crew in and sign for the move.

### Between semesters

Summer internships and study-abroad terms often leave a gap between leases. We can coordinate short-term storage so you're not paying for an empty apartment. See [storage between homes](moving-storage-austin.html).

### Keep it simple

- Pack in small boxes—they fit stairs and elevators best
- Label boxes by room and keep valuables with you
- Photograph the old apartment when it's empty for your deposit

unpacking-services-austin.html.h1: Unpacking that gets you home sooner.
unpacking-services-austin.html.lede: The move isn't done when the truck is empty. Our crew can unpack rooms, set up furniture and take the packing materials away.
unpacking-services-austin.html.article:
## The part of moving everyone forgets

Most people unpack the kitchen and bedroom, then live around boxes for weeks. Unpacking help turns that into a day.

### What unpacking can include

- Unpacking boxes into the right rooms, cabinets and closets
- Reassembling beds, tables and other furniture
- Placing furniture according to your floor plan
- Collecting packing paper and empty boxes

### Pick the rooms that matter most

Kitchens take the longest to unpack and make the biggest difference. Many people have the crew handle the kitchen and bedrooms, then finish the rest themselves.

### Make it smooth

Label boxes with the room and a short list of contents, and decide where major pieces go before moving day. It's faster when the crew doesn't have to guess.

Pair it with [packing services](packing-services-austin.html) for a true door-to-door, full-service move.

antique-art-movers-austin.html.h1: Antiques and art, moved like they’re irreplaceable.
antique-art-movers-austin.html.lede: Old finishes, fragile joinery, framed art and family heirlooms get extra protection, careful packing and a crew that never rushes.
antique-art-movers-austin.html.article:
## Why antiques need a different approach

Old wood dries out, veneers lift, glue joints weaken and original finishes scratch easily. Antique pieces often weigh more than they look and have weak points that aren't obvious until something goes wrong.

### Art, mirrors and glass

Framed art and mirrors travel on edge, never flat, with corner protection and padding. Large or very valuable pieces may need custom packing—tell us the size and type in advance.

### Clocks and delicate mechanisms

Grandfather and wall clocks need weights and pendulums removed and secured before they move. If you're unsure how, ask before moving day.

### Document before the move

- Photograph valuable pieces from several angles
- Note existing scratches, chips or repairs
- Ask about liability limits and consider extra coverage—in Texas, it's agreed in writing before the move

For pianos and organs, see [piano moving](piano-moving-austin.html).

side.title: Tell us about
side.text: Details for a safe plan.

faq.q: Do you move antiques and fine art?
faq.a: Yes. Delicate and valuable pieces get extra padding, careful packing and an unhurried carry.

faq.q: Should I insure valuable items?
faq.a: Mover liability is agreed before the move and isn't the same as insurance. For high-value pieces, consider separate coverage.

faq.q: How are paintings and mirrors moved?
faq.a: On edge, padded and corner-protected, never laid flat. Very large or valuable pieces may need custom packing.

in-home-furniture-moving.html.lede: New flooring, a remodel, home staging or just a new layout: we move heavy furniture room to room or floor to floor without damaging walls, floors or backs.
in-home-furniture-moving.html.article:
## When you need furniture moved but aren't moving

Some of the heaviest lifting happens without a change of address. Common reasons:

- New flooring or carpet installation
- Kitchen, bathroom or room remodels
- Staging a home for sale
- Moving a piano, armoire or bed upstairs or downstairs

### Protecting the house

Doorways, stair rails and floors take the most damage when heavy pieces move inside a home. We pad furniture, protect floors and corners, and take pieces apart when that's safer.

### Remodels and flooring

Coordinate with your contractor on timing: furniture usually needs to come out of the room the day before work starts and go back once floors have cured. Short-term storage can help if rooms will be out of action for a while—see [storage between homes](moving-storage-austin.html).

### Staging for sale

Realtors and homeowners often need furniture removed, rearranged or brought in for listing photos. Tell us the plan and the deadline.

moving-checklist.html.h1: The moving checklist, from eight weeks out to settled in.
moving-checklist.html.lede: Enter your move date to see a target date for every stage, tick tasks as you go, and print it for the fridge.
moving-checklist.html.article:
## How to use this checklist

Start as early as you can. Eight weeks is comfortable for a house; an apartment move can compress the first stages into two or three weeks. If you're short on time, focus on the essentials: book the mover, reserve elevators and parking, and keep documents and medication with you.

## The tasks most people forget

- **Building rules.** Elevator reservations, loading-dock hours and insurance certificates at both addresses.
- **Parking.** In Austin, a truck in a metered space or curb lane may need a City permit—call 3-1-1.
- **Texas paperwork.** Update your driver license address within 30 days of moving, plus your vehicle registration and voter registration. See the [Texas change-of-address checklist](change-of-address-checklist-texas.html).
- **The freezer.** Defrost it a day ahead so it doesn't leak in the truck.

## Let the crew take tasks off the list

A full-service move covers packing, disassembly, loading, transport and setup. See [all moving services](services.html) or the [moving day guide](move-day-guide.html).

faq.q: How far in advance should I start planning a move?
faq.a: About eight weeks ahead for a house, and three to four weeks for most apartments. Book the mover early for summer and end-of-month dates.

faq.q: What's the most important thing to do first?
faq.a: Book a licensed mover and get a written proposal, then reserve elevators, docks and parking at both addresses.

moving-box-calculator.html.h1: How many moving boxes do you need?
moving-box-calculator.html.lede: Choose your home size and how much you own to get a starting list of boxes, tape and packing paper.
moving-box-calculator.html.article:
## Which box for what

- **Small boxes:** books, tools, canned goods, records—anything heavy
- **Medium boxes:** kitchen items, toys, small appliances, linens
- **Large boxes:** pillows, lampshades, bedding and other light, bulky things
- **Wardrobe boxes:** hanging clothes, straight from the closet
- **Dish-pack boxes:** double-walled boxes for dishes, glasses and fragile kitchenware

## Packing tips that prevent damage

Keep each box under about 50 pounds, fill empty space with paper so nothing shifts, and tape the top and bottom seams. Label two sides and the top with the room and contents. For more, see [how to pack like the pros](packing-services-austin.html).

## Why most people run short

Kitchens, garages and closets always hold more than expected. Buy a few extra small boxes—they're the first to run out—and keep unused ones to return or pass along.

side.title: Box rules of thumb
side.text: Quick guidance.
items: Label two sides and the top

faq.q: How many boxes do I need for a two-bedroom apartment?
faq.a: As a starting point, about 25 small, 20 medium and 10 large boxes plus a few wardrobe and dish-pack boxes. Use the calculator to adjust for how much you own.

faq.q: What size box should books go in?
faq.a: Small boxes. Books get heavy fast, and small boxes keep the weight manageable and safe to carry.

faq.q: Can the movers pack for me?
faq.a: Yes. Our crew can pack the whole home, just the kitchen and fragile items, or anything in between.

moving-cost-calculator.html.lede: Get a quick planning range for a local or Texas move, then request a written estimate for a price based on your actual move.
moving-cost-calculator.html.article:
## What this calculator does—and doesn't—do

It gives a planning range based on typical crew sizes and hours for each home size, plus mileage for moves elsewhere in Texas and common add-ons. It's a starting point for your budget, **not a binding quote**.

## What makes a real quote different

Your written proposal accounts for what a calculator can't see: stairs and elevators, the distance from the truck to the door, how much is packed, large or fragile items and your date. See [how moving quotes work in Texas](moving-quotes-texas.html).

## Ways to keep costs down

- Declutter before the move—less to pack and carry
- Pack non-fragile rooms yourself and leave the kitchen to the crew
- Have everything packed and ready before the crew arrives
- Reserve elevators and parking so no time is lost on the day
- Choose a mid-month, mid-week date if you have flexibility

side.title: For a written estimate
side.text: Share these details.

faq.q: Is the calculator result a quote?
faq.a: No. It's a planning range. Your written estimate is based on the details of your move, and Texas movers must give you a written proposal before loading.

faq.q: What affects the cost of a move most?
faq.a: The amount you're moving, access at both homes, distance, extra services like packing, and timing.

faq.q: How can I lower my moving cost?
faq.a: Declutter, pack what you can, have everything ready on time, and choose a mid-month weekday if possible.

change-of-address-checklist-texas.html.lede: Who to tell, and by when, after a move within Texas—driver license, vehicle, mail, voting and utilities.
change-of-address-checklist-texas.html.article:
## Required by Texas

### Driver license or ID: within 30 days

Texas requires you to change the address on your driver license or ID card within 30 days of moving. You can do it online, by mail or in person. Source: [Texas DPS](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/how-change-information-your-driver-license-or-id-card).

### Vehicle registration

Update the address on your vehicle registration with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles so renewal notices reach you. A USPS change of address does **not** update TxDMV records. Visit [TxDMV](https://www.txdmv.gov/).

### Voter registration

Update your voter registration address so you can vote at your new polling place. Start at [VoteTexas.gov](https://www.votetexas.gov/).

## Mail and accounts

- File a change of address with [USPS](https://moversguide.usps.com/)
- Banks, credit cards and insurance (home, auto and health)
- Employer and payroll
- Subscriptions, deliveries and online stores
- Doctors, dentists, pharmacy and veterinarian
- Schools and childcare

## Utilities in the Austin area

- **Electric:** inside the City of Austin, service is through Austin Energy; elsewhere, your provider depends on the address—ask your landlord, builder or the previous owner
- **Water, wastewater and trash:** usually your city or local utility district
- **Gas:** if the home has gas service, schedule a start date
- **Internet:** book installation early; appointments can be weeks out

Schedule shut-off at the old home for the day after you move out, and start-up at the new home for the day before you arrive.

side.title: Key deadlines
side.text: For moves within Texas.
items: Voter registration: before the next election

faq.q: How long do I have to change my driver license address in Texas?
faq.a: Thirty days after moving, according to the Texas Department of Public Safety. You can update it online, by mail or in person.

faq.q: Does a USPS change of address update my vehicle registration?
faq.a: No. Update your vehicle registration address with the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles separately.

faq.q: When should I set up utilities at my new home?
faq.a: Schedule them one to two weeks before your move, with service starting the day before you arrive.
